items.title: Freshness SLAs by cadence, with an `ok | quiet | stale | broken` verdict
items.detail: Cadence is declared per source rather than one flat deadline for all of them: `CADENCE_DAYS` (src/freshness.js:101) gives each source a `cadence_days` and a `min_expected_delta`, so `noaa_enso` (35) and `who_gho` (730) are judged on their own publication clocks while the on-demand sources carry `cadence_days: null` and are given no deadline to miss. `explainVerdict` returns one of `ok | quiet | stale | broken | never_run` (src/freshness.js:64), and the four-way distinction is the item: a working source with nothing to report (`quiet`) and a dead source (`broken`) used to report the same string, which is how a healthy food-security pipeline and a broken one looked identical from the status route. The verdict reaches `GET /api/v1/ingest/status` as a `verdict` object beside the legacy `status` string (src/ingestion.js:988), and `sourceHealth()` at src/ingestion.js:1189 — replacing rather than breaking, so existing consumers of `status` keep working.

items.title: Per-source data assertions with quarantine-on-fail
items.detail: Assertions are data, not code: `SOURCE_ASSERTIONS` declares per-source `required_fields`, `value_range`, `coordinate_bounds`, `monotonic_dates` and `min_count_vs_trailing` rules as frozen plain objects (src/assertions.js), so a test can read the map, count it, and require that nothing is declared without being measured. A batch that fails is withheld from its live collection and written to a `quarantine_<collection>` store instead, carrying the failures that condemned it (src/store.js, src/schema.js) — six quarantine collections, one per ingestable collection, with `test/ingestion-wiring.test.js` asserting the list covers `OUTPUT_COLLECTIONS` in both directions so a new collection cannot be added without either its quarantine home or a failure. The run reports `degraded` with the assertion text rather than the previous silent `store.merge`. Wiring this surfaced the falsy-zero trap twice in one afternoon: `Number.isFinite(Number(null))` is `true` because `Number(null) === 0`, so every null-valued field passes a `Number.isFinite` filter — the first fix appeared to work and did nothing, and it is now pinned by an explicit test. It also caught a defect in the guard rather than the data: the lite `conflict_csv` format has no identifier column, so requiring `source_id` quarantined 100% of documented uploads. The normalizer now mints one from the same fields the id is minted from and flags `source_id_minted` so nobody reads it as an upstream key.

items.title: Watermarks, incremental fetch, resumable backfill
items.detail: Shipped. `src/watermarks.js` (27 tests) implements the per-source watermark, incremental fetch windows, resumable backfill cursors and the resume-after-crash case, and it is now wired into three consumers: `src/connectors/open-meteo-flood.js:14`, `src/connectors/open-meteo-archive.js:14` and `src/routes/provenance.js:36` (`describeWatermarkState`). Watermark state is a declared collection, read once at the start of a run and written back only for sources that reported a position, so an interrupted run keeps its cursor (`test/watermark-persistence.test.js`). The audit's before-state: nothing called the module, the two archive connectors defaulted `endDate` to today and re-walked from 1981 on every run, minting a fresh id daily, and `gdacs-archive.js` was a synchronous loop with no progress or resume.
items.note: src/watermarks.js is pure — state in, state out, nothing stored — and the connector contract already accepted and returned `options.watermark_state` / `output.watermark_state`. Nothing supplied either end, so a 40-year archive walked its whole series on every run and re-downloaded it to discover nothing was new. Now a declared collection, read once at the start of a run and written back only for sources that reported a position, so an interrupted run keeps its cursor instead of losing it. Backfills resume through `resumeBackfill` and report through `backfillProgress`. test/watermark-persistence.test.js: the second run resumes from what the first stored; an unwired connector keeps its position rather than resetting it; sources do not read each other's.

items.title: Source-agreement cross-validation
items.detail: Shipped in three parts, because the item named three gaps and each was a different kind of work. `src/agreement.js` computes what the item asks for — Pearson and Spearman correlation, a paired-month floor of three, a sign-disagreement rate capped at 0.25, and a four-value verdict of `agree | marginal | disputed | unavailable` — and pairs on `period`, never on array index, so a one-sided hole does not shift every later month against the wrong partner. `src/geotiff.js` is the minimal GeoTIFF reader the item's own text calls for: stripped, single-band, uncompressed or deflate, with the horizontal predictor undone, and it refuses every combination it does not implement by naming the tag rather than returning a plausible grid. `src/connectors/chirps.js` reads pixels through it and writes a real `precipitation_mm` per region per day (the record used to carry `null` on every row, so there was nothing to compare), bounded by a decode cap that counts attempts rather than successes. `src/source-agreement.js` is the half that was missing between the engine and the store: it knows which `source` values are two measurements of the same rain (`chirps` against `open_meteo_archive` as ERA5), turns the daily records into monthly totals while dropping a month reported too thinly to be one, and serves it at `GET /api/v1/source-agreement` in the derived family, which reports its refusals and names the sources it left out and why. No winner is declared between the products, by the spec's own words.
items.note: src/agreement.js, src/geotiff.js, src/connectors/chirps.js, src/source-agreement.js. Coverage is its own axis with its own vocabulary, one-sided months named rather than counted: `unmatched_months` compared two sizes, so two products covering twelve disjoint months each differ by zero — a clean bill of health for a comparison that never happened. 'these two disagree' and 'only one covers this' no longer both arrive as `unavailable`. The route reports `refused` per region and a verdict tally, so a region with one product present cannot read as agreement, and it names each skipped source (a forecast, a discharge series, a Pacific SST index) with the reason rather than dropping it silently. No winner is declared, by the spec's own words. test/source-trust.test.js, test/source-agreement-route.test.js.

items.title: Connector health scoring and circuit breaking
items.detail: The breaker is reached: `runIngestion` gates each source through `allowRequest` before it fetches, and an open circuit produces `status: 'skipped'` with `verdict` naming the reason — reported distinctly from `ok` and from `broken`, because a skip is not a success and not a failure, it is 'we did not look'. Failure streak was previously computed at src/ingestion.js and read nowhere else; it now opens the circuit after three consecutive failures, with a half-open probe and a cooldown. `src/circuit.js` also scores each source on latency, success rate and payload drift. Both of the caveats this entry used to carry are now measurably false, corrected 2026-10-16 rather than left standing. (1) "the breaker state is per-run, so it does not survive a process restart" — `connector_circuit` has been in `SCHEMA` since `cdadc81` (2026-10-05), `runIngestion` writes it back through `store.merge` (`src/ingestion.js:605`) and reads it at the top of the next run (`:198`), and `ingestionStatus` reports `circuit.persisted` so a reader can tell a durable breaker from a per-run one instead of being shown `closed` and reading it as healthy. Measured on the demo store: `persisted: true`. (2) "the health score is computed but not surfaced on any route" — it is a field of every row `ingestionStatus` returns (`src/ingestion.js:1063`, scored over the persisted breaker's own retained outcomes) and `/api/v1/ingest/status` serves that array whole, so the score is reachable. Measured by calling `ingestionStatus` directly: the row carries `health` with a non-null `success_rate`, and `latency_samples` is non-zero against real runs — all 611 `source_runs` in the demo store carry `diagnostics.duration_ms`, which is what `outcomesFromRuns` reads, so the score is measurable in production rather than permanently null.
items.note: src/circuit.js. closed -> open on three consecutive failures -> half_open after the 30-minute cooldown -> exactly one probe, which closes or re-opens with the cooldown restarted. Recovery is asserted reachable in both directions; `opened_at: null` never probes. scoreConnector scores the breaker from STORED run history via outcomesFromRuns, not the in-memory window runIngestion rebuilds and discards per run — it previously existed only in tests. A breaker skip is not a success. test/connector-circuit.test.js.

items.title: Enforce the rate limits that are already declared
items.detail: Shipped. `src/rate-limit.js` (578 lines) — the token bucket, concurrency cap, jitter, `parseRetryAfter` and `createBudget` — is enforced rather than exported: `fetchWithRetry` acquires from a per-source, per-host limiter before every attempt and releases it in a `finally` (`src/connectors/http.js:256`), so a retry takes a second token instead of holding the only one across its backoff. The IPC fan-out is capped at the declared `concurrency: 2` (`src/connectors/ipc-hdx.js:278`, read from `RATE_LIMIT_POLICIES.ipc_hdx`), which is what its `rateLimit: { perMinute: 20 }` at `:443` now means; the audit's 'unbounded `Promise.all` at ipc-hdx.js:265' is that comment line, and `:311` is the bounded worker pool. The API limits itself through `src/inbound-rate-limit.js`, wired at `src/server.js:484` and answering 429 with a `retry-after` header at `:620`. The two remainders this entry used to name are now closed, both in `distributeReport`'s neighbourhood rather than the connector seam. Its webhook branch carried no `AbortSignal`, so a partner that accepted the connection and never answered held the request that triggered the distribution open indefinitely; it now runs under one 5 s deadline spanning the response *and* its body (`src/routes/reporting.js:84`, `:672`), because a server that sends headers and then stalls aborts inside `readExternalResponse` rather than inside the fetch — measured, and a `.catch` on the fetch alone leaves that case uncovered. The timeout is translated into a message naming the budget rather than the runtime's bare `TimeoutError: The operation was aborted due to timeout`, which names the mechanism and not the deadline and is what would otherwise land in the run row an operator reads. And `createBudget` — correct, tested, and called from nothing but its own test file — now bounds ING-06's walk: `gdacs_archive` declares `budget_ms: 900000` in `SOURCE_POLICIES` (`src/source-policies.js:54`), `runIngestion` passes it through as a request field (`src/ingestion.js:226`), and the connector spends it across the walk and checks it before each window (`src/connectors/gdacs-archive.js:86`), recording `budget_ms`, `windows_skipped_by_budget` and `budget_exhausted` on the verdict and naming the stop in `errors`. Absent the declaration the walk is unbounded, so the deadline is opt-in and the policy table stays the one place a budget is stated. 15 minutes is about four times the slowest run observed across every source in the demo store (`ipc_hdx`, 174.8 s) while still bounding the 168-quarter walk that reaches ~4.2 h. The RapidPro client timeout it also asked for is live (`src/rapidpro.js:417-423`).
items.note: fetchWithRetry acquires from a per-source, per-host token bucket before every request (src/connectors/http.js), so the rateLimit blocks in the connector specs and connectors.registry.json stop being documentation. A headerless 429 now waits for whichever is longest of Retry-After, the bucket's next token, or the backoff — a 500 says nothing about anyone's rate budget, so only 429 consults the limiter. ratePerWindow and windowMs can be overridden per call, which is what makes a refill assertable without waiting out a 60-second window. test/rate-limit-wiring.test.js: bursting, per-host budgets, holding a budget across calls, releasing the slot when a request fails, and refusing an unreadable declaration rather than inventing a limit.

items.title: Raw payload retention, replay, and fixture seeding
items.detail: `src/capture.js` (27 tests) plus `scripts/capture-fixtures.mjs` implement raw-payload retention, content-addressed fixture seeding and replay: `withCapture` wraps a fetch, stores the body, and can serve it back so a connector test replays bytes instead of mocking `globalThis.fetch`. The fixture capture path exists and can be run. What does not exist is the call site: no connector is wrapped in `withCapture`, so nothing is actually retained in production and no fixture in test/fixtures/ was produced by the script — they remain hand-assembled, which is the reason the capture exists.
items.note: src/capture.js. RETENTION_POLICY states the window in one place and renders it into log lines, store files and the CLI's own output. Pruning leaves a tombstone that round-trips through the store file, and ReplayPrunedError is distinct from ReplayMissError: 'we captured it and policy took it' and 'we never captured it' are different facts. Every replay carries a provenance stamp with deliberately no `unstamp`. Replay through fetchWithRetry now carries tombstones too. test/capture-retention-replay.test.js, test/capture-cli.test.js.

items.title: Bitemporal records
items.detail: Every upstream-revisable collection now keeps the value it replaced. `mergeById` still overwrites by id — that is correct for the live set — but `JsonStore.merge` (src/store.js:124) now calls `supersededVersions` before the overwrite and merges the result into a new `record_versions` collection, so `valid_from`/`valid_to` intervals plus the previous body survive. `valueAsOf(collection, id, when)` reconstructs what the platform believed at a past instant, and `changedFields` names which fields moved. Two decisions worth stating. `NON_SEMANTIC_FIELDS` excludes `updated_at`, `ingested_at`, `generated_at` and `last_run_at`, because otherwise every daily re-ingest would report a revision and the history would be noise. And `versionRow` sets `payload_hash: null` deliberately: the body being stored is the predecessor's, and carrying the incoming hash would make `mergeById` drop the history row as a duplicate of the record it describes. A record with no timestamp at all produces no history row — the overwrite still happens, and the platform declines to lie about when.

items.title: Completeness tripwires for capped pagination
items.detail: Shipped. `src/completeness.js` implements the pagination bookkeeping the item asks for — pages fetched, records seen, provider-declared total, whether the last page was full, and a `possibly_incomplete` flag when a cap bit before a floor rather than after one — and three consumers read it: `src/ingestion.js:21` (`COMPLETENESS_VERDICTS`, `completenessVerdictName`), `src/connectors/gdacs-archive.js:5` (`assessPagination`, `mergeCompleteness`) and `src/connectors/chirps.js:3` (`assessPagination`, `recordCap`). The verdict is a run-record field, a scanned flag and a status-route verdict, read before the assertion pass can replace the output (`test/pagination-completeness.test.js`). The audit's before-state: nothing called the module, `gdacs-archive` walked quarter windows keeping only the feature count, and `chirps` applied its 30-record cap without recording what it dropped, so a truncated walk was indistinguishable from a quiet upstream.
items.note: The verdict is a run-record field, a scanned flag and a status-route verdict — read BEFORE the assertion pass can replace the output, because a quarantined batch drops every non-collection key, which is exactly when an operator most needs to know. test/pagination-completeness.test.js.

items.title: Record-level provenance with real transform versions
items.detail: All four defects this item listed are closed. `upstream_url_or_endpoint` is the URL actually fetched, not a constant null: `fetchWithRetry` records every fetch against the current run (src/connectors/http.js:18), which is the only place the retrieval URL is knowable at all, since no connector exposes the URLs it builds internally. `transform_version` is derived from the connector function's own body hash (`transformVersionFor`, src/provenance.js:112) and moves when the parser moves, rather than being the typed-in `'0.1.0'`. Each published record is stamped `_source_run_id` at ingest, and the lineage loop filters on it — previously it rebuilt a run-wide union inside the per-run iteration, so a nine-source run wrote nine identical rows each describing all nine. Provenance is read back from `record._source_run_id` rather than recomputed, so the attribution travels with the record instead of being re-derived from a set that has since changed.
